transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess I came in because I’ve been having some thoughts I’m not really proud of. It’s not like I’ve made a plan or anything to hurt myself, I haven’t. But sometimes I catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just… didn’t wake up. I know that probably sounds bad.
Are you wanting to kill yourself right now?

No… not right now. I don’t want to kill myself. It’s more like… I keep having these thoughts that maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. But I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself or anything like that.
Did something stressful happen in your life before these thoughts started?

Yeah… I mean, I did get fired, and that was pretty stressful. Right after that, though, I kind of felt… I don’t know, almost fired up? Like I was going to prove everybody wrong. But I guess I was also more irritable than I’d like to admit—snapping at people over little things, like at the coffee shop. It wasn’t anything terrible, I don’t think… but yeah, that happened before the thoughts got worse.
During that fired-up period after losing your job, did you need less sleep than usual?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but there were a few nights where I only slept maybe two or three hours. And then I’d get up feeling… fine, actually. Like I had a full tank, no reason to slow down. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During that fired-up period, did you feel more confident or powerful than usual?

Yeah… I guess so. I mean, not like I thought I was Superman or anything. But I did have this feeling that I could walk into any store in the district and run it better than the managers there. Like getting fired somehow made me the one who really knew how things should be done. Does that make sense?
During that fired-up period, were you more active than usual—starting lots of projects or taking on more than normal?

Yeah, I guess I was… busier than normal. I tried to keep it productive, you know? I was bouncing around between job applications, rewriting my resume, and then I’d get an idea for some woodworking project and start sketching that out too. I probably wasn’t sitting still long enough to actually finish one thing before jumping to the next. That’s… that counts, right?
During that fired-up period, did your behavior cause serious problems in your life?

Yeah… I mean, I tried to tell myself it was just a rough patch, you know, after losing the job. But it did cause problems. I fell behind on some bills, and I missed a couple callbacks and appointments I really shouldn’t have missed.

I kept meaning to stay on top of the job search, but I couldn’t keep it steady. Even stuff at home got kind of sloppy, more than usual. I don’t like admitting that, but it got to the point where I knew I wasn’t just going to fix it by trying harder, if that makes sense.
About that fired-up period after you lost your job, did it last for at least a week?

Yeah… it did. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it was, but it was more than a few days. That stretch was probably about three weeks after I got fired, where I was kind of running high and not really in control of it. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During that three-week high period, were you talking more than usual?

Yeah… maybe a little more than usual. I mean, I didn’t think of it as a problem at the time. At the chess table, though, people would kind of laugh and tell me, “Take a breath,” because once I started explaining my comeback plan, I guess I just kept going. The words were just… coming out fast. Does that make sense?
During that three-week high period, did your thoughts feel like they were racing?

Yeah… I guess they were. I didn’t really call it “racing” at the time, but my mind was jumping around pretty quick — like from sales numbers, to job leads, to some beer recipe idea, then suddenly to an old argument I hadn’t thought about in years.

It was hard to hold onto one thought for more than a few seconds. I’m not sure if I’m explaining that right, but it felt like everything was moving too fast in my head.
During that three-week high period, did you have any experiences where you were hearing or seeing things that other people couldn’t?

I mean… not seeing things, no. Hearing, maybe. I don’t want it to sound too strange, but there was one time I was sitting alone in my kitchen and I heard my old store manager’s voice, like clear as day over the store intercom, telling me to “move the display.”

I knew I wasn’t at the store, obviously, so I kind of brushed it off at first. But it did feel real in the moment. Does that count as what you’re asking?
Before this current low period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed for days or weeks like this?

I’m not sure… not really like this, I don’t think. I mean, I’ve had bad days, like anybody, maybe a rough week here or there, but I don’t know that I’d call it the same kind of depressed.

I don’t want to overstate it, you know? This one feels more… noticeable, I guess. Does that answer what you mean?
During that three-week high period, did you believe you had special abilities or importance that other people would have said wasn’t true?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t know if I’d call it “special abilities,” exactly. That sounds a little grand.

But for a while I really did feel like I could walk into any store in the district and run it better than the managers there. Like somehow losing my job had made me see everything more clearly, like I was the one who knew how it should all be done.

At the time it felt confident, not weird. Looking back, I can see maybe other people would’ve thought I was getting ahead of myself. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
